title: Enterobacter cloacae cystitis on ceftriaxone, no fever or upper tract signs, nothing by mouth

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), case list approved by the owner

clinical_review.notes: Owner clinical review: cases look good.

story: A 74-year-old woman on postoperative day 2 after hip fracture repair develops dysuria and frequency without fever, flank pain or bacteremia; she has no indwelling urinary catheter. She has an ileus and takes nothing by mouth. Urine grows Enterobacter cloacae complex, resistant to the usual oral agents; she is on IV ceftriaxone.

problems.title: Closed fracture of the femoral neck

reference_answer: No AmpC finding: IDSA 2026 limits its caution about ceftriaxone for moderate-risk AmpC organisms to invasive infections, and this is cystitis without upper tract or bloodstream involvement. Its preferred agents for AmpC cystitis (nitrofurantoin, TMP-SMX) are resistant or cannot be taken by mouth; a single-dose aminoglycoside is a listed alternative a pharmacist may suggest, which is outside what the AmpC rule addresses.
rationale: The negative pair of the Enterobacter bacteremia case. IDSA 2026 (Question 2.4) limits its caution about ceftriaxone for moderate-risk AmpC organisms to invasive infections, so the AmpC rule must stay silent here; a rule that fires on organism and drug alone, ignoring the site, fails this case. IDSA 2026 does not list ceftriaxone among its agents for AmpC cystitis; the choice of agent is outside the rules this case tests. IV to PO does not apply: she is not taking anything by mouth and no susceptible oral agent exists.

citations.supports: AmpC-producing Enterobacterales: ceftriaxone for uncomplicated cystitis versus invasive infections; cefepime when the MIC is 2 or lower.

Current version: Question 2.4 limits the ceftriaxone caution to invasive infections; Question 2.7 prefers nitrofurantoin or TMP-SMX for AmpC uncomplicated cystitis, with a single-dose aminoglycoside among alternatives; checked against IDSA's published 2026 text and approved by the owner, 2026-11-12.
Prospective audit and feedback of antibiotic therapy as a stewardship intervention.
